title: A commit's own closing keyword never actually closed the PR
author: off-by-one
description: Compares the repository's default-branch commit history against its own pull request set: a commit names a real GitHub closing keyword (close/closes/closed, fix/fixes/fixed, resolve/resolves/resolved, both tenses) for a PULL REQUEST that is still open well after that commit landed. The PR-side twin of commit-closes-keyword-issue-still-open, which explicitly only ever checked issue numbers -- GitHub's own auto-close/auto-merge-adjacent trigger fires against a referenced pull request the same way it fires against an issue, so a commit naming a PR number with a real closing keyword makes the identical promise, and that promise can silently never fire exactly the same way.
confidence_notes: Age-gated on how long the commit has sat on the default branch while the named PR stays open, not flat -- the identical shape commit-closes-keyword-issue-still-open uses, deliberately not deviated from. Under 24 hours scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden -- GitHub's own auto-close/auto-merge-adjacent trigger can lag a few minutes behind a push, and nobody expects a PR to have closed within the hour). At or past 24 hours it scores a flat 0.85 -- an unambiguous, non-fuzzy signal: a real closing keyword landed on the default branch and the target PR is still open a full day later. No genuine reason found to trust a PR-side resolution signal less than an issue-side one (duplicate-pr-still-open reached the identical conclusion for its own issue/PR twin pair), so this recipe keeps the sibling's exact bar rather than inventing a new one. A commit naming no closing keyword, naming a PR number that does not exist in this repo (a broken link, not this recipe's own seam), or naming an already-resolved PR (merged, or closed without merging -- either way the promise already held) is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- the identical discipline every recipe before this one holds.
